name: Universal Solar, LLC
old_description: Stable electricity is one of the most recurrent problems of rural areas. At Universal Solar, LLC, we want to help our customers to enjoy power even when there are blackouts. We’re a solar company serving in Millersburg, PA, with almost a decade of experience in the industry. We take pride in providing our customers with energy-efficient solutions for their properties. If you’re looking for a trusted solar company in Millersburg, PA, you’re in the right place!
about:
Universal Solar, LLC is a solar installation and service company based in Millersburg, Pennsylvania. The company has been operating for nearly a decade, focusing on energy-efficient solutions for rural areas prone to blackouts. The business is operated by Elmer, who is frequently cited in customer reviews for his hands-on expertise and responsiveness.

The company designs and installs off-grid, grid-tied, and grid-interactive solar systems for residential, commercial, and industrial clients. Its service portfolio includes solar panel installation and repair, battery storage solutions, system maintenance and inspection, and well pump installations. Universal Solar serves a multi-county region in central and northeastern Pennsylvania, including Millersburg, Bloomsburg, Lewisburg, Williamsport, and Scranton.

Customers range from homeowners seeking backup power to businesses and industrial facilities aiming to lower energy costs. Commercial projects include roof-mounted arrays for businesses, while industrial installations target facility-scale energy production.

Universal Solar was motivated by the vulnerability of the electrical grid and aims to help customers achieve energy independence. The company offers free estimates and financing options to reduce upfront costs.

name: Uptown Millworks
old_description: Uptown Millworks is a New Orleans millwork shop and furniture maker specializing in quality, style and function. We work to make a comfortable, personal environment from every client's needs. The finishing touch of beauty and personality for any room.
about:
Uptown Millworks operates from the Uptown neighborhood of New Orleans, Louisiana, as a locally owned and operated custom millwork shop. The company was founded by Christian Pokorn, who comes from a multi‑generational woodworking family in Austria and spent summers in his family’s sawmill. After building a career in construction as the principal of Pokorn Construction, Pokorn established Uptown Millworks to focus on custom architectural millwork and historically faithful restoration for New Orleans homes.

The shop produces a full range of millwork and furniture, including handrails, flooring, cypress slabs, custom cabinets, moldings, windows, doors, shutters, and turnings. Using time‑tested woodworking techniques alongside modern precision tools, the team of millwrights, carpenters, and woodworkers fabricates every piece in their New Orleans workshop.

Uptown Millworks serves residential, hospitality, and commercial clients across Louisiana, with projects in private homes, restaurants, hotels, and historic buildings. The company coordinates directly with customers and vendors on architectural millwork, casework, and restoration work that meets the standards of the Architectural Woodwork Institute, the Forest Stewardship Council, and the NOLA Historic District Landmarks Commission.

Pokorn emphasizes building with honor and integrity, describing quality as the company’s entire philosophy. The operation prioritizes local manufacturing to create jobs, sources FSC‑certified and sustainable woods, and delivers finished pieces with its own crew to keep the carbon footprint low. Offcuts and sawdust are repurposed in the shop or donated to community gardens and animal shelters, reflecting a commitment to resource stewardship.

about:
Urth Apparel Inc. is a custom apparel manufacturer based in Newport Beach, California. Founded in 2013, the company began as an international trade cooperative focused on natural foods and cotton apparel from Peru. The founder started the venture after struggling to find a factory that shared a passion for fashionable products beyond basic tees and cared for the environment and workers.

The company provides end-to-end product development and manufacturing services, including fashion and technical design, fabric and trim sourcing, pattern making, grading, marker making, sampling, cutting and sewing, screen printing, sublimation, heat transfer, finishing, packaging, and inspection. Production is split across three origins: luxury clothing in Italy, knitwear and basics in Peru, and specialty technical apparel in the USA. Urth Apparel runs dedicated production lines for tees, tanks, and polos, and emphasizes sustainable and organic materials. The team consists of three employees at the Newport Beach headquarters, coordinating with overseas factories.

Urth Apparel serves clothing brands of all sizes, from startups to established labels, across categories such as tees and tanks, dresses, kids and baby apparel, yoga and athleisure wear, swimwear, and dress shirts. The company works with brands seeking a one-stop partner for concept-to-market apparel production, offering daily communication between design teams in the USA and Europe and production floors abroad.

The founders created Urth Apparel because they were unhappy with existing manufacturing partners that delivered non-uniform quality, poor business practices, and high minimums. Their philosophy centers on doing it right: taking care of the planet, taking care of workers, and creating clothing that lasts. The company positions itself as an ethical clothing factory that makes sustainable manufacturing easy for brands.

The firm buys and sells new, used, obsolete, and hard-to-find electrical equipment, with a focus on circuit breakers, hardware kits, transformers, safety switches, bus plugs, MCC buckets, and starters. name: Utility Wire Products
old_description: Utility Wire Products, Inc. specializes in Point of Purchase Display Racks. We can produce a rack from your design, or work with you to develop a design, anything from a single display rack to meet a one product display need or a whole group to fill up a Plan-O-Gram for your product line.
about:
Utility Wire Products, Inc. operates from a 48,000-square-foot facility on Cleveland's industrial East Side, at 3302 East 87th Street. The company was founded in 1953 by Ed Peck and Bill Milavac. Donald Anzells purchased the business in 1980 and has led it as a family-owned, trans-generational operation; his son Ronald Anzells serves as president after 30 years with the firm, and Ronald Anzells Jr. joined in 2007 as plant manager and custom tooling specialist.

The shop specializes in custom wire forming across five major product lines: point-of-purchase display racks, wire guards for lighting, fans, machinery and heaters, wire baskets, wire forms, and grids. It works wire diameters from .080 to .500 inch in bright basic, stainless steel, and galvanized wire, and incorporates tubing, sheet metal, and plastics. An on-site 3D CNC bending machine supports both prototyping and production runs of 1 to 500,000 units. Finishing options include powder coating, vinyl, nylon, and various platings.

Customers span retail chains needing plan-o-gram display systems, industrial OEMs requiring protective guards, medical facilities using baskets for hospital stretchers, and manufacturers sourcing wire forms for screw-machine parts. The company accepts orders as small as a single unit and scales to high-volume production.

The firm's stated philosophy is to deliver a "Quality Product in a Timely Fashion at a Fair Price that are American made," treating every order — whether one piece or half a million — with equal importance and personal attention.

name: V-Tron Electronics Corporation
old_description: Manufacturers of High-Quality Assemblies, Wire Harnesses, Box Build, and Fiber Optic Assemblies
about:
V-Tron Electronics Corporation, based in Attleboro, Massachusetts, was incorporated in 1970 as a privately held, veteran-owned small business. The company began as an electronics service provider to the emerging Massachusetts computer industry in the 1970s before expanding into semiconductors, medical, military, and industrial electronics. President Doug Gobin emphasizes that quality and reliability are keys to survival in a competitive market.

The company manufactures custom cable assemblies, wire harnesses, fiber optic assemblies, molded connector assemblies, and box build integrations in a 45,000-square-foot facility. Processes include low- and high-pressure molding with PVC, polyurethane, polypropylene, TPE, and TPA; fiber optic termination; and full box build with sheet metal chassis. V-Tron handles low to high volume order lot sizes, using a real-time bar-coded ERP system to track jobs from order inception through final inspection. Every assembly undergoes 100% functional testing, with Cirris 4250 scanners automating electrical tests on cables and harnesses.

V-Tron serves defense and security, military, life sciences, medical, semiconductor, and industrial electronics customers. Its assemblies are built to IPC standards in an ISO 9001:2015 environment, with UL and cUL recognition (E76510, E173242) and CSA certification (LR56498-1). The in-house training program, led by an IPC-certified instructor, ensures associates meet J-STD-001, IPC-A-610, and IPC/WHMA-A-620 workmanship requirements.

Founded on the principle that quality cannot be inspected into a product, V-Tron differentiates itself through reverse engineering and pre-production manufacturability analysis, a functional guarantee on every harness, and a culture of continuous improvement driven by its quality management system.

name: VIP plastics and rubber manufacturing
old_description: Vip Rubber and Plastic is one of the best rubber and plastic manufacturing facilities in America. We specialize in custom rubber extrusions, plastic extrusions, rubber sheet products, molded rubber products, plastic pipe and tubing. We have been manufacturing high-quality parts in the USA since 1961.
about:
Vip Rubber and Plastic operates from Minden, Nevada, where it has been manufacturing rubber and plastic products since 1961. The company was founded by Howard Vipperman Sr., known as “Big Vip,” who entered the rubber industry as a gasket cutter after serving in the armed forces. It remains a family-owned business led by subsequent generations.

The facility produces custom and standard rubber extrusions, rubber sheet and rolls, molded rubber parts, and custom rubber compounds. On the plastic side, it runs plastic extrusion lines for profiles, pipe, tubing, vinyl spline, and window and door seals. A merger with Excalibur Extrusions expanded its plastic extrusion capacity. The company also offers value-added fabrication under its Vip+ Services banner, positioning itself as a one-stop shop.

Its customer base spans agriculture, aerospace, automotive, architectural glass and metal, and construction. The aerospace segment includes approvals to several Boeing material specifications, and the quality system holds AS9100 certification. The company notes it has produced parts for virtually every industry over its history.

Vip Rubber and Plastic emphasizes honesty and integrity as core values, and highlights its domestic manufacturing—all products are made in the USA. The founder’s hands-on experience on the shop floor is cited as the foundation for the company’s technical depth and long-term customer relationships.

The company was acquired in 2011 by Jessica Dambrackas, who purchased the business from its previous incarnation as Rutland Industries.

The company runs a 12,000-square-foot facility with climate-controlled warehousing and loading docks. Its services span kitting, packaging, and assembly (including hand assembly), pick-and-pack order fulfillment, e-commerce integration, warehousing, cross-docking, quality control, distribution, and inventory management.

VMS serves electronic manufacturers, food packaging companies, e-commerce retailers, fashion labels, and publishing houses such as the Rutland Herald.

Dambrackas established a mission to employ as many individuals with disabilities as possible, and the company operates on lean manufacturing principles. VMS also emphasizes fixed pricing to simplify forecasting and offers e-commerce software that connects to shopping carts within minutes.

about:
Valley Woodcraft & Lumber Co., based in Wilkes-Barre, Pennsylvania, was founded in 1952. The company operates as a small, veteran-owned contract manufacturer serving a range of industrial sectors.

The shop produces custom wood, phenolic, composite, and machined plastics components, delivering everything from single parts to fully assembled products built to print specifications. Its process capabilities include CAD/CAM design, CNC machining with nested-based production, drilling, finishing, profiling, sanding, shaping, mortise-and-tenon joinery, laminating, gluing, fingerjointing, paraffin treatment of lumber, and both commercial and Mil-Spec packaging. The facility offers standard, express, and urgent delivery options to meet varying lead-time requirements.

Valley Woodcraft serves customers in aerospace, aviation, defense, furniture, maritime, rail, transit, transportation, construction, and utilities. The company’s quality system is certified to ISO 9001 and AS 9100 for the manufacture of high-precision machined parts used in defense, aviation, aerospace, transportation, and other industries.

The firm emphasizes assured product quality, competitive pricing, on-time delivery, and the flexibility to fulfill orders of any size. Its veteran-owned status and dedicated team with advanced technology are cited as key differentiators that enable rapid response to urgent customer needs.

old_description: The Valley Woodworkers of West Virginia cares about our community and does what we can to improve it.  The mission of the Valley Woodworkers of West Virginia is twofold.  One part is the training of local community members to be woodworker. about:
Valley Woodworkers operates from Dunbar, West Virginia. The organization was founded in 2008 and functions as a woodworking club open to all skill levels. Its origins trace to a dual mission: training local residents in woodworking crafts and producing heirloom-quality wooden toys for the Salvation Army’s Christmas distribution to underprivileged children, a program ongoing since 1991.

The club holds monthly meetings on the second Thursday at its clubhouse on 12th Street, featuring project show-and-tell sessions and technical demonstrations. The facility serves as a gathering point rather than a commercial production shop; no headcount, square footage, or output volumes are published.

Participants range from beginners to professional woodworkers, while the toy program benefits children served by the Salvation Army. Local businesses such as Woodcraft and Withrow Supply in Huntington provide sponsorship and material support, including finishes, machinery, hardware, and sharpening services.

The group emphasizes community improvement through skill-sharing and charitable giving. Its distinguishing feature is the long-standing commitment to producing handcrafted toys for children in need, coupled with an open-door policy that welcomes anyone with an interest in woodworking.

name: Valley Woodworks LLC
old_description: Most furniture is manufactured to be replaced. Engineered composites, spray-on finishes, metal fasteners hidden beneath a surface that mimics wood without being it. It looks fine on day one. By year three, it shows you exactly what it was.
about:
Valley Woodworks LLC is a custom furniture maker based in Palmer, Massachusetts. Founded in 2022 by Jonathan Dias, a Springfield College graduate with a background in business administration and entrepreneurial studies, the company began from his desire to create high-quality, handcrafted pieces that avoid the disposable nature of mass-produced furniture.

The shop produces custom tables and furniture using solid hardwood slabs selected for grain, moisture content, and character. No veneers, plywood cores, or shortcuts are used; each piece is finished with hand-rubbed hardwax oils that protect the wood while keeping its pores open and grain visible. Operations are carried out on a made-to-order basis, with no stated facility size or employee count beyond the founder.

Valley Woodworks serves residential clients seeking heirloom-quality dining tables, desks, and other furniture pieces. The company does not list specific commercial or industry clients, focusing instead on individual commissions that start with a design consultation.

Dias started the business to counter the click-to-buy culture and preserve the art of fine furniture making. The company emphasizes that its pieces are built to be passed down rather than replaced, a philosophy reflected in the choice of solid materials and traditional finishing methods.

Vault Furniture operates from Caldwell, Idaho, where it was co-founded by designer Brandi. The company began as a maker of reclaimed-wood furniture and has grown into a high-end manufacturer of handcrafted shelving, desks, tables, and home accessories.

The business was founded on a pledge to create heirloom-quality furniture from sustainably sourced materials while providing exceptional customer service. Differentiators include free custom design support with co-founder Brandi, free shipping and exchanges within the contiguous United States, and a commitment to 100 percent U.S. handcrafting.

about:
Velmar Food Services operates from Phoenix, Arizona, where Richard and Judith Barton founded the family-owned company in 1974. The business traces its recipes to Richard's father, who applied his culinary craftsmanship to develop the perfect burrito. Now a third-generation family-run enterprise, Velmar has grown from supplying mobile food services to serving unified school districts across Arizona and California.

The company manufactures its Arizona Gold brand of Mexican cuisine — including burritos, appetizers, entrees, side dishes, and desserts — using locally produced tortillas, robust beans, cheese, green chiles, fresh eggs, and choice meats. In addition to production, Velmar runs a foodservice distribution operation that stocks breakfast, lunch, center-of-the-plate entrees, and desserts from top labels. Its warehouse and freezer facilities also provide pallet storage leasing for other food businesses needing seasonal or overflow capacity.

Velmar's customers include restaurants, delis, convenience stores, healthcare facilities, correctional operations, and school districts throughout Arizona and California. The Arizona Gold line has become a staple in school meal programs, while the distribution side supplies a broad range of foodservice operators through local distributors.

Velmar emphasizes cultural authenticity and flavor maximization while minimizing cost, a philosophy rooted in the founding family's recipes. The company differentiates itself by combining manufacturing, distribution, and warehousing under one roof, allowing customers to simplify procurement from a single source. Community involvement, including sponsorship of local charities, is also cited as a core value.

Vermillion Inc. was established in 1965 in Wichita, Kansas. The company operates a 43,000-square-foot manufacturing facility in the city.

Vermillion specializes in custom cable solutions, including bulk cable production, custom-designed cable assemblies, and molded assemblies. The facility produces cables with conductor ranges from 0 to 28 AWG using materials such as tinned, nickel-plated, and silver-plated copper. Shielding options include the proprietary Vermalloy® alloys, Aracon® aramid fibers, and various foil and Mylar configurations. Jacketing materials span high-temperature ETFE, PTFE, PFA, low-smoke zero-halogen polyethylene, and braided or blown-on jackets made from Nomex, Kevlar, PEEK, Viton®, and other polymers. The company emphasizes engineering consultation and serves as a resource for prototype and initial production runs.

The primary markets are military and aerospace. Vermillion has been recognized by Rockwell Collins as Wire and Cable Supplier of the Year multiple times, most recently noted in 2009. Its products meet stringent defense and aviation standards, supported by certifications to ISO 9001 and AS9100.

Vermillion differentiates itself through its proprietary Vermalloy® shielding material, described as the most effective secure-voice shielding available, and through in-house certified trainers for J-STD-001 soldering specifications.

name: Vermont Electric Power Company
old_description: VELCO is the owner/operator of Vermont’s high-voltage transmission system and does not directly serve individual homes and businesses. We deliver the power to your local distribution company which then delivers it to you.
about:
Vermont Electric Power Company (VELCO) is headquartered in Rutland, Vermont. The company was created in 1956 as the nation’s first statewide, transmission-only utility, formed to build and operate an interconnected high-voltage grid that would deliver and share access to clean power, including hydroelectric resources, across Vermont. Ownership is structured uniquely: the company is held by the state’s 17 distribution utilities and a public benefits corporation, with a for-profit model designed to return value to those owners, their customers, and all Vermonters.

VELCO owns and operates Vermont’s high-voltage transmission system, delivering bulk electricity to local distribution utilities rather than directly to homes or businesses. Its core activities include grid operation, maintenance, and planning to ensure a reliable, affordable, safe, secure, and sustainable transmission network. The company also provides a unified voice on regional energy issues. While specific facility sizes and headcount are not disclosed, VELCO serves the 17 member distribution utilities that collectively supply power throughout the state.

The primary customers are those 17 distribution utilities, which include municipal departments such as Barton Village Electric Department, Burlington Electric Department, Hardwick Electric Department, and others listed in the company’s public materials. Indirectly, VELCO’s transmission services support every electricity consumer in Vermont. The company operates within the electric power transmission and clean energy sectors, with a stated focus on environmental stewardship and sustainability.

VELCO differentiates itself through its pioneering transmission-only structure, its ownership model that aligns incentives with public benefit, and its mission to serve as a partner. The company emphasizes safety as a core value, publishes an annual ESG report, and promotes a culture of belonging and innovation to advance a sustainable energy future for Vermont.

about:
Virginia Food Works operates a VDACS-inspected commercial kitchen at the Prince Edward County Cannery in Farmville, Virginia. The nonprofit organization was established to support Virginia farmers by providing a rental production facility for small-batch commercial retail co-packing during harvest season.

The facility offers appointment-based access to licensed equipment including kettles, mixers, fillers, and canners, with trained staff assisting clients through hot-fill, water-bath, and pressure canning processes. Production runs are scheduled Thursday through Saturday on a first-come, first-served basis, with peak demand from June through December. The kitchen specializes in acid and acidified foods—such as sauces, jams, relishes, and syrups—made from locally grown produce like tomatoes, berries, apples, peppers, and ginger root. Because of its regulatory scope, the facility cannot handle products containing meat, fish, or dairy.

Virginia Food Works serves both Virginia and out-of-state farmers looking to preserve seasonal harvests and reduce waste, as well as emerging small-business food entrepreneurs navigating commercial production for the first time. Clients range from growers creating value-added products for retail markets to startups needing guidance on recipe scaling, regulatory compliance, and process authority reviews. The organization also assists with VDACS registration and food safety training requirements.

The nonprofit's resource-first approach aims to strengthen Virginia's food system by helping producers transform perishable crops into shelf-stable goods that can be sold year-round, expanding market opportunities for local agriculture while keeping more food production within the state.

old_description: This rare vinegar is dark red and heavy bodied with a rich nose. It goes well with bold, mixed greens and blue cheese. Particularly good in a meat marinade or to add structure in marinara sauces and stews
about:
Virginia Vinegar Works is based in Shipman, Virginia, and has been producing artisanal vinegars since 2008. The operation began with wine vinegar made in porcelain crocks and has since expanded to stainless steel tanks and oak barrels for aging.

The company crafts wine vinegars, seasonal fruit vinegars, and malt vinegars using the traditional Orleans method, a slow conversion process that preserves the character of the base wine. Production involves stainless steel tanks for fermentation and older wine barrels for aging, after which barrels are selected for blends or single-varietal bottlings. Fruit vinegars combine rich wine vinegar with fresh fruit from nearby farms, while malt vinegars are made from local craft beer, yielding a robust, umami-rich product. The lineup includes varietal-specific vinegars such as Cabernet Franc, Chardonnay, Petit Verdot, and Albariño, as well as blended heritage red and white wine vinegars, white balsamic, sherry vinegar, and malt vinegar.

Virginia Vinegar Works serves professional chefs, restaurants, gourmet food outlets, and home cooks seeking exceptional flavor. Its products are marketed for both culinary and gift use, with direct shipping to customers. The company also offers consultation services.

The business was born from a desire to add exceptional flavor to the great local produce and meats available in central Virginia. The founders emphasize that the slow Orleans method and barrel aging retain the original character of the wine, creating vinegars with richness and depth that rapid commercial processes cannot achieve.

old_description: Another step in empowering more industries with intelligent power distribution East Greenwich, April 12, 2024 – VoltServer, a leading provider of Digital Electricity™ (DE), Fault Managed Power solutions, has attained Cisco Select Developer status. This accomplishment demonstrates VoltServer’s expertise and solidifies its position as a trusted and valued collaborator within the industry. The collaboration between VoltServer and Cisco opens new opportunities for both companies to drive innovation in efficient and sustainable power delivery solutions. With VoltServer’s proven expertise in Digital Electricity™ combined with Cisco’s leadership in the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) technologies, the companies are driving advancements in powering industrial and outdoor environments where traditional power sources are limited or inaccessible. VoltServer’s Digital Edge Solutions, combined with Cisco’s IIOT platforms, enable enterprise-grade connectivity in even the most rugged and challenging spaces. Together, they empower organizations to deploy Cisco IE Series Power over Ethernet (PoE) switches deeper into their networks, delivering enhanced efficiency, connectivity, and performance. “We are very excited to become a trusted powering solution for Cisco’s IIoT solutions,” states Matt Giuliano, EVP and GM, Emeritus, Communications and In-Building at VoltServer, “and to continue to work with Cisco’s engineering teams to collectively address joint go-to-market opportunities in several strategic vertical markets including extended campus & outdoor spaces, ports and airports, utilities and oil & gas.” The attainment of Cisco Select Developer status marks a significant milestone for VoltServer as they continue their 10-year deployment history as the industry’s pioneering leader in Fault Managed Power, via their Digital Electricity platform. “We are driven by innovation and are proud to be setting the standard in Fault Managed Power Systems. Together, with our valued partners, we are solving the world’s power distribution demands and building solutions to create a better future for us all,” says Stephen Eaves, CEO and Founder at VoltServer.
about:
VoltServer is headquartered in East Greenwich, Rhode Island. The company was founded by Stephen Eaves, who serves as CEO, and has a 10-year deployment history as of 2024. Matt Giuliano holds the role of EVP and GM, Emeritus, Communications and In-Building.

VoltServer develops and manufactures Digital Electricity™ (DE), a patented fault-managed power system classified as Class 4 under the 2023 National Electrical Code. The technology splits energy into packets transferred from a Transmitter unit to a Receiver unit, with safety monitoring after each packet. The company reports more than 1,000 building installations and 40,000 circuits across large venues.

The company serves telecommunications service providers deploying 5G and Wi-Fi networks, transportation hubs such as ports and airports, enterprise buildings and campuses, industrial manufacturing facilities, data centers, and building electrification projects. VoltServer also collaborates with partners including Cisco, where it holds Select Developer status for IIoT power solutions, and Eaton for critical infrastructure.

VoltServer states its technology reduces installation time by using existing data pathways and hybrid fiber cable, lowers material costs by eliminating conduit, and improves safety by halting hazardous current within milliseconds. The platform is designed for energy efficiency and can qualify for LEED credits. The company says it is driven by innovation and aims to set the standard in fault-managed power systems.

WC Woodworks, Hardwoods, & Sawmill operates from Ocala, Florida, where it has been a family-owned business since 1987. WORLD electronics is headquartered in Reading, Pennsylvania. The company was founded in 1991 and became a Rado family business in 1986 when Joe Rado purchased it. Wei Chuan serves retail grocery chains, food-service distributors, and consumers across North America. Its Food Service and Groceries categories supply restaurants, institutions, and supermarkets, while the Natural, Organic, and Vegetarian line targets health-conscious shoppers. The Dumpling King series, launched in the early 1990s, remains a flagship retail product.

The founders started the business because authentic Chinese flavors were unavailable in the U.S. market. Today, Wei Chuan emphasizes continuous investment in technology, rigorous quality control, and recipes that balance tradition with innovation, aiming to make “comprehensive flavors” accessible to every household.

old_description: More than 25 acres contain a solar array of approximately 21,000 fixed-tilt, ground-mounted photovoltaic solar panels. Electricity generated is distributed through purchase agreements with local utility Chickasaw Electric Cooperative and Tennessee Valley Authority.
about:
The project originated in 2009 when a $62.5-million allocation from the American Recovery and Reinvestment Act was awarded to the Tennessee Department of Economic and Community Development. The University of Tennessee Research Foundation was contracted to oversee creation and operation of the facility, which was designed and built by Signal Energy, LLC of Chattanooga in 2011, with grid connection achieved in early 2012.

The farm comprises approximately 21,000 fixed-tilt, ground-mounted photovoltaic panels generating electricity sold under purchase agreements to Chickasaw Electric Cooperative and the Tennessee Valley Authority. Alongside power production, the SPECTRUM exhibit provides hands-on learning stations, games, and QR-linked resources to teach solar energy basics to students, homeowners, and business visitors. The exhibit partners include Oak Ridge National Laboratory, the Tennessee Valley Authority, and multiple state agencies.

The facility serves utilities, educational institutions, and the general public. Its electricity feeds the regional grid through TVA and Chickasaw Electric Cooperative, while the exhibit attracts school groups, science-fair participants, and homeowners exploring rooftop solar. Partners such as the U.S. Department of Energy, Tennessee Advanced Energy Business Council, and Volkswagen reflect a broad stakeholder base spanning government, research, and industry.

The project was conceived as a dual-purpose asset: a revenue-generating solar array and a public showcase for renewable energy technology. Its backers emphasized job creation, education, and technology commercialization as core goals, positioning the site as a living laboratory for solar adoption in Tennessee.

Westinghouse Electric Co LLC is headquartered in Hopkins, South Carolina. The company traces its origins to 1869 when George Westinghouse founded Westinghouse Electric, beginning a legacy of engineering innovation that later extended into nuclear energy.

Today Westinghouse designs and supplies nuclear reactor technology, fuel, and services for the global nuclear fleet. The company reports approximately 12,500 employees across more than 100 locations in 23 countries, and supplies over 100,000 nuclear parts annually.

Its technology underpins 57 percent of the world's operating nuclear reactors, and the company maintains nearly two-thirds of the global fleet while fueling 40 percent of it. Recent projects include conditional purchase orders with Polish suppliers for the first AP1000 unit at Lubiatowo-Kopalino, full clevis bolt replacement at Sweden's Ringhals plant, and delivery of the final ITER vacuum vessel sector.

The company's founding principle—making technology better, faster, and more efficient—remains its differentiator. Westinghouse supplied the world's first commercial pressurized water reactor in 1957, and its technology remains the basis for roughly half of today's operating reactors. about:
Wisconsin Metal Parts operates from Waukesha, Wisconsin. The company was founded in 1988 as Die Concepts, Inc. and renamed Wisconsin Metal Parts in 2010 to reflect its expanded services. In 2024, it was acquired by SOLV Metals, joining a larger group of metal manufacturers while retaining its management team and skilled workforce.

The shop provides integrated metal fabrication, CNC machining, wire EDM, metal stamping, tool and die making, and assembly services under one roof. Its fabrication equipment includes fiber laser cutting, CNC punching, CNC bending, CNC forming, welding, and hardware insertion. Wire EDM handles electrically conductive materials up to 16 inches thick, with dedicated carbide-cutting capacity running 24/7. CNC turning offers bar feeding to 3-inch diameter, a 25.6-inch swing, and parts up to 40 inches long by 14.3 inches in diameter. Stamping presses run up to .188-inch thick, specializing in high-volume, tight-tolerance work from .003 to .060 inch thick, producing nearly 60 million stampings annually at a 98% on-time delivery rate.

Customers span aerospace, agriculture, foodservice, medical, military/defense, and the container industry. The company handles projects ranging from military ordnance mechanical fuzes and shell casing machining to steel detent plates and stainless steel dispensing nozzles, serving both prototype and production quantities across low-to-high volume, high-mix runs.

Wisconsin Metal Parts emphasizes intellectual value and the "Golden Rule" in its mission: minimizing risk, delivering high-value solutions, and building trust through open communication. Its cross-trained workforce maintains workflow flexibility, while in-house tool design uses forming and stamping simulation software to validate designs before die construction.

about:
Wisconsin Wire Works, Inc. was founded in 1994 in Wales, Wisconsin, by five copper-industry veterans who set out to produce copper and copper alloy welding wire.

The firm operates as an integrated manufacturer of welding consumables, drawing wire from base stocks sourced from established suppliers. Its facilities house state-of-the-art drawing equipment and an in-house welding laboratory staffed by welding engineers, metallurgists, and fabrication specialists. Products include aluminum bronze, silicon bronze, deoxidized copper, phosphor bronze, copper alloy brazing wires, and nickel aluminum bronze, supplied in precision layer-level wound spools, straightened-and-cut lengths, reels, coils, and barrel packs. All wire undergoes thorough inspection for size, cleanliness, cast, and helix before shipment.

The company serves welders, fabricators, and manufacturers across industries that rely on automatic and robotic welding, with customers on every continent.

Wisconsin Wire Works emphasizes customer-driven quality: drawing dies are reworked on a fixed schedule rather than only when worn, non-contaminating lubricants are used exclusively, and products are cleaned and packed in hermetic moisture-barrier cartons. The quality system is certified to ISO 9001:2000, and the company highlights its made-in-the-USA origin as a core differentiator.

Its product lines include growth control systems, plating systems, and bone void fillers. Its single-use kit model aims to reduce infection risk, eliminate set processing, and decrease hospital setup and processing time, enabling more children to receive proper treatment each day.

about:
Wolfe Custom Woodworking LLC operates from Englewood, Colorado, serving the Denver metropolitan area. The company was founded by Daniel E. Wolfe, who has spent many years crafting fine furniture and cabinets before establishing the LLC.

Materials include white oak, North American black walnut, Indian rosewood, and vinyl for casework applications.

Past projects include a white oak banquette and dining table, a walnut banquette, a mid-century modern media credenza, a solid walnut bookshelf, a shaker hutch, and a modern side table featuring a bookmatched Indian rosewood top. A client testimonial describes a custom walnut barn door for a master bathroom.

Wolfe emphasizes direct client involvement in the design process, believing that custom work should reflect each customer’s exact vision. He cites a passion for creating pieces that clients will use and love for years, and differentiates the shop by personally handling every stage of design and fabrication.

old_description: We embrace challenges, persevere through obstacles, and never give up until our goals are achieved. We are ready to lend a hand, learn new processes, and take ownership of our work. We lead by example and show passion, curiosity, and pride in everything we do.
about:
American Woods traces its roots to 1979 when Wood Products Inc. began as a cabinet shop serving Innes Construction in Grand Forks, North Dakota. The business expanded into commercial cabinetry, and in 1982 Lowell and Georgia Innes founded American Woods to meet customer demand for matching hardwood accessories. The two entities merged under the American Woods name in 2003, combining custom cabinetry with a growing line of wood goods under single ownership.

Today the company operates a roughly 160,000-square-foot furniture manufacturing facility in Grand Forks with a workforce of about 100. The plant runs milling, machining, sanding, sawing, sub-assembly, finishing, and final assembly lines, producing a wide range of home furnishing products from real hardwoods and premium materials. Daily truck shipments move finished goods to distribution points across the country.

American Woods supplies finished furniture to multiple nationally recognized brands, including long-standing partner Room & Board (producing the Berkeley, Copenhagen, and Danbury lines) and former mass-market programs for Target, Costco, and Lowe's. The company also works directly with resellers seeking luxury furniture solutions and maintains its own branded collections.

The business emphasizes American-made craftsmanship, consistency, and efficiency, framing its differentiation around enduring partnerships, a made-in-America promise, and a team culture built on pride and integrity.

Raphael founded the company to avoid the impersonal nature of bulk distribution and assembly-line construction, emphasizing sustainability and personal service. Customers range from weekend warriors to serious enthusiasts who need custom sawn lumber for personal projects. The service area covers hobbyists and small-scale builders across western Wisconsin who bring their own logs for processing.

The goal is to save clients time and money not only at the sawmill but throughout their subsequent projects.

old_description: Max H. Ries, a German immigrant who operated a textile firm in his native Munich, left Germany in 1939 and had intended to develop a similar company in Chicago. about:
World Finer Foods is headquartered in Bloomfield, New Jersey. The company traces its roots to 1947 when German immigrant Max H. Ries founded Reese Finer Foods after arriving in the United States in 1939. Originally intending to establish a textile business, Ries pivoted to food importing and built the Reese brand into a specialty-food label.

Today the firm manages and markets more than 60 premium food, beverage and personal-care brands encompassing over 1,000 products. It operates as a full-service distributor and brand manager, providing sales representation, trade and consumer marketing, finance processing (order management, invoicing, promotional spend, deductions and collections) and end-to-end logistics including EDI, FDA compliance, inventory control and warehousing on an Oracle ERP platform. The company serves as the exclusive U.S. customer for its brand partners, selling to more than 350 retail and distribution accounts.

Its client base includes domestic and international specialty-food producers such as Barry’s Tea, Marmite, Bonne Maman, Dr. Woods and London Pub, as well as its own heritage Reese line.

The business was built on the principle that a collective network of producers, importers and distributors could grow together. That relationship-driven philosophy remains central, underscored by membership in the Specialty Food Association, The Food Institute and status as the only U.S. member of the Circle of European Specialty Food Distributors (CEISA).

about:
Zero Manufacturing is headquartered in North Salt Lake, Utah, and traces its origins to 1931 when German immigrant Herman Zierold established a small sheet-metal shop in Los Angeles after designing a rugged aluminum case to protect his engineering documents in the California oil fields. The business evolved through several ownership changes and was later renamed Zero Manufacturing Co. in 1959. Today the company operates under the leadership of Rockwood Equity Partners and CEO Declan McLaughlin.

The company specializes in mission-critical protective cases and enclosures made from high-strength aluminum and advanced polymers. Its 286,000-square-foot Utah facility houses deep-drawn aluminum forming, rotomolding, laser cutting, CNC punching, certified welding, anodizing, powder coating, and assembly operations. With 145 team members, Zero produces more than 270,000 parts annually across 2,600 unique SKUs and has manufactured over 5 million products since inception.

Zero serves aerospace and aviation, defense and military, medical, energy/oil & gas, industrial, electronics & infrastructure, and logistics sectors. Its cases have protected equipment ranging from Apollo 11 moon-rock containers to avionics, field-deployed medical diagnostics, and downhole sensors in harsh oilfield environments. Customers include NASA, major defense contractors, medical device OEMs, and industrial equipment manufacturers.

Zero positions itself as an engineering-led manufacturing partner that combines disciplined engineering, vertically controlled domestic production, and long-term partnership. The company emphasizes predictable lead times, consistent quality through ISO 9001-certified processes, and expert guidance from concept through testing — often at no cost — to deliver protection where failure is not an option.

Zenith Electronics LLC is headquartered in Lincolnshire, Illinois. Founded in 1918, the company began with the advent of radio. Since 1999, it has operated as a wholly owned subsidiary of LG Electronics, serving as LG's U.S. research subsidiary for consumer electronics, hospitality, health care technologies, and broadcasting standards.

Today, Zenith functions as a technology development and licensing organization. Its researchers create encryption and broadcast technologies, most notably Pro:Idiom, a digital television encryption system widely deployed in the hospitality industry. The company administers licensing for Pro:Idiom, offering royalty-free agreements to qualified partners.

Zenith's technologies serve the consumer electronics, hospitality, health care, and broadcasting sectors. Hotel operators and digital TV providers implement Pro:Idiom to secure premium content delivery. The company's broadcast standards work supports terrestrial HDTV transmission, while its health care and consumer electronics research feeds into LG's global product lines.

The Zenith name has been associated with electronics innovation since 1918. Company records cite a legacy of firsts: the first wireless TV remote control, the first portable and push-button radios, the first stereo audio systems for FM radio and television, and the first terrestrial broadcast system for HDTV using digital technology. That heritage of pioneering standards continues to drive its licensing and research mission.

83 MetalCraft LLC operates from Garden City, Idaho, in the Boise metropolitan area. The company was founded in 2016 and expanded its presence to Boise in 2021. Ownership details and founder names are not publicly disclosed.

Core processes include cutting, shaping, welding, finishing, and installation of steel components. The company fabricates railings, handrails, grabrails, gates, fencing systems, window well covers, security doors, and ornamental ironwork. The business was started to avoid the shortcuts and low-margin practices common in larger shops, emphasizing structural-grade construction with reinforced framing, precision welding, and protective coatings designed for Idaho's heavy snow loads and temperature swings. 8th Avenue Food & Provisions is headquartered in Minneapolis, Minnesota. The company was founded in 2018 through the strategic combination of Post Holdings' private-brands businesses, creating a dedicated platform for private-label and branded food manufacturing. In 2025, Post Holdings completed its acquisition of 8th Avenue and merged it with the Post Consumer Brands segment, while the company's pasta business — formerly Dakota Growers Pasta Co. — was transferred to Richardson Food & Ingredients effective December 1, 2025.

The company produces nut butters, granola, dried fruits, nuts, and trail mixes across seven facilities in the United States and Canada. Plants in Fitzgerald, Georgia; Troy, Alabama; Blaine, Washington; Markham, Ontario; and Brampton, Ontario focus on nut butter. A Eugene, Oregon site makes granola, and a Hazelwood, Missouri facility handles fruits and nuts. 8th Avenue describes itself as one of the largest private-label nut butter manufacturers in North America, with in-house roasting and seasoning capabilities and decades of production experience.

Its customer base spans retail, food-service, and ingredient channels. The company supplies private-label programs for national and regional brands, providing custom formulations that include organic and non-GMO granola options as well as conventional and organic peanut and tree-nut butters.

8th Avenue emphasizes a rigorous supplier-approval program, food-safety systems, and supply-chain efficiency as its operational differentiators. The business was created to give brand owners a single source for on-trend, high-quality private-label foods backed by responsive service.

Notable projects include work for Longwood Gardens, the University of Delaware’s Caesar Rodney Dining Hall Complex, and projects with The Whiting-Turner Contracting Company and EDiS Company.

The company emphasizes creative solutions that minimize cost and lead time, and it is consistently recognized in the industry for meeting high work and safety standards for its employees.

A & I Distributors is headquartered in Mandan, North Dakota, and traces its roots to 1924 when Frank Stanaway founded the business in Butte, Montana. Since its founding, the company has emphasized building lasting customer relationships through consistent product quality and knowledgeable service. name: A C Power Tech Inc
old_description: Our extensive electrical knowledge and mining experience have combined to bring valuable, customized products and services to our customers since 1998.
about:
A C Power Tech Inc. operates from Belle Vernon, Pennsylvania, where it relocated after initial operations in nearby Donora. The company was founded in 1998 by Alex Cerreti, who brought 18 years of maintenance management experience at Helen Mining Company and more than four decades of hands‑on expertise troubleshooting electrical substations and high‑voltage transmission lines. Cerreti remains president and still performs on‑site service and repair when needed.

The firm manufactures and rebuilds power distribution centers, electrical distribution boxes ranging from single‑circuit cable extenders to multi‑circuit enclosures, and high‑voltage switch gear (vacuum switch houses) in single, dual, and triple output configurations for surface and underground use. It also builds variable‑frequency drives, reduced‑voltage soft starters, and across‑the‑line starters across any horsepower range, integrates them into belt load centers, and develops PLC systems to mesh with existing controls. A specialty line includes portable power supplies for low‑voltage tools and communications in remote areas, plus engineered electronic devices designed to replace legacy mining equipment.

Primary customers are in the mining sector — coal mines, stone quarries, and salt mines — with additional work for food and beverage processors. The company supplies both new and remanufactured power centers, belt starters, distribution boxes, portable power supplies, and high‑voltage switch gear, and provides turn‑key electrical substation installations, circuit‑breaker testing and calibration, and a multifunction power‑center circuit tester used by MSHA and the Pennsylvania DEP.

Cerreti founded the business to combine deep mining‑industry electrical knowledge with customized product development, emphasizing rapid troubleshooting — often resolved by telephone — and application‑specific engineering such as isolated dual switch houses and 2,500 kVA underground substations.

Accu-Mold Plastics was founded in 1972 by Jack L. Strohecker and his wife Mary Lou in the basement of their Halifax, Pennsylvania home. Originally named Accu-Mold & Tool Company, the business began as a precision mold and die operation serving the electronics industry. Early clients such as American Catheter Company and Hamilton Watch helped the shop expand beyond tooling into injection molding, and by 1973 the company had installed its first automatic molding machine.

Today the company operates a 9,000-square-foot facility equipped with automated injection molding presses ranging from 22 to 125 tons of clamping force and shot capacities of 1.2 to nearly 9 ounces. Its in-house tool room provides CNC machining, sinker EDM, surface grinding, manual machining, and heat treating, supporting complete mold design, construction, and repair. A geothermal-controlled clean room enables contamination-free molding for medical and electronic components, while overmolding and insert molding capabilities allow multi-material assemblies. The shop handles everything from single-cavity prototypes to full-scale production runs, with value-added services including assembly, packaging, and just-in-time delivery.

Accu-Mold serves the electronics and medical device sectors, with a historic focus on medical disposables and start-up companies needing high-quality molds to compete against larger rivals. Current customers include firms in electronics and medical disposables, though specific names are not disclosed.

The company emphasizes efficiency, competitive pricing, and customer support, leveraging modern molding technologies and streamlined processes to keep clients competitive. Its founding vision was to deliver high-quality precision molds and components to the electronics industry, a mission that has expanded to include comprehensive in-house design, tooling, and molding under one roof.

about:
Luvata Waterbury operates from a facility on Thomaston Avenue in Waterbury, Connecticut. The business traces its roots to 1971 with the founding of Intermagnetics General Corporation (IGC). Outokumpu Copper Products Oy acquired IGC Advanced Superconductors in 2001 and rebranded the operation as Luvata in 2006. Mitsubishi Materials Corporation purchased Luvata in May 2017, making the Waterbury site a subsidiary of the Japanese materials group.

The plant specializes in manufacturing copper-stabilized niobium-titanium (NbTi) and niobium-tin (Nb3Sn) conductors for low-temperature superconducting applications. Its product line covers superconducting wire and cable used in magnetic resonance imaging systems, particle accelerators, and fusion energy research. The site employs a team of over 100 professionals focused on innovation and production excellence.

Customers span medical diagnostic imaging, high-energy physics, and nuclear fusion sectors. Luvata Waterbury superconductors have been specified for the Large Hadron Collider at CERN, the KSTAR fusion research project in Korea, the International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor (ITER), and a $6.5 million supply contract for CEA Saclay in France. A $26 million U.S. Department of Energy fusion contract was awarded in 2009.

The company positions itself as a recognized leader in superconductive wire supply where delivery and performance are critical. Its selection for flagship international science projects and long-standing ISO 9001 and ISO 14001:2015 certifications underscore a focus on quality and environmental management.

Acue-Tex Inc operates from a 6,000-square-foot facility in Hubbard, Oregon, just south of Portland along I-5. The Terrells attribute the company's longevity to honesty, transparency, and a personal commitment to getting things right. In-house tooling capability and a focus on recycled materials further distinguish the operation.

Promotional offers such as 15% off $35 and 20% off $100+ are available for online orders.

old_description: is a leading, full-line manufacturer of cable ties and wiring accessories proudly made in the USA.
about:
Advanced Cable Ties, Inc. operates from Gardner, Massachusetts, where it has produced cable ties and wiring accessories for over 30 years. The company describes itself as a full-line manufacturer focused on designing and building the strongest fasteners in the world, with all engineering, tooling, and material processing handled in-house.

The firm manufactures standard and specialty cable ties, mounts, abrasion protection, and conductivity products, supported by advanced tooling and material processing capabilities. It maintains a large inventory of military-grade materials and offers same-day shipping on stocked items, backed by a 100% quality guarantee. Quality assurance testing and compliance with UL Type 21S, CSA Type 21S, and military standard AS33671 are integral to its production.

Advanced Cable Ties serves military, industrial, and electrical sectors, providing cable management solutions that meet NEMA application guides. The company sells exclusively through authorized distributors and supports customers with regional managers and manufacturers' representatives. Its products are used in applications requiring high tension, temperature, and weather resistance.

The company emphasizes its vast inventory, rapid availability, quality certifications, and product longevity as key differentiators. Its stated objective is to design and manufacture the strongest cable ties globally, a mission supported by ISO 9001:2015 registration and a commitment to building strong partnerships with distributors and end users.

Advanced Electronic Solutions operates from Alpharetta, Georgia, in the Atlanta metropolitan area. The company provides electronic manufacturing services spanning design, assembly, testing, and logistics.

The firm delivers a full suite of engineering and manufacturing capabilities. Engineering services include product design and development, printed circuit board layout, and prototyping. Manufacturing covers surface mount technology (SMT) assembly, through-hole (THT) assembly, mixed-technology PCB assembly, box build integration, cable and wire harness assembly, and mechanical assembly. Component sourcing and procurement support the production line. Testing services encompass in-circuit test (ICT), functional test, burn-in, and environmental stress screening (ESS). After-sales support includes return, repair, and warranty services.

The company serves other businesses requiring electronic component and assembly manufacturing, from prototype samples to mass production volumes. No specific industry verticals are disclosed.

Advance Electronic Solutions states its mission is to facilitate every customer's electronic product manufacturing needs from design through shipping. It emphasizes continuous improvement in quality, delivery, technology, and cost, and aims to make the journey from sample manufacturing to mass production as easy and convenient as possible.

name: Advanced Food Equipment, LLC
old_description: Since 1990, AFE has been providing a full array of exceptional cooling, freezing and processing equipment.
about:
The company began with a focus on designing and manufacturing hygienic spiral and tunnel cooling and freezing solutions for the food processing industry. A new corporate office was built in Ridgway in 2020, and a European office opened in Uden, Netherlands, in 2014.

AFE engineers and manufactures a range of industrial freezing and cooling equipment, including spiral freezers, IQF tunnel freezers, plate freezers, blast freezers, spiral coolers, spiral steamers, shakers, and clean-in-place (CIP) systems. Fabrication employs robotic welding, laser cutting, 3-D modeling, and automatic bending equipment to produce stainless-steel components. The company also provides installation, repair, preventative maintenance, spare parts, and in-house or on-site product testing using its AFE Field Test Unit.

The equipment serves food processors across baked goods, dairy, seafood, pasta and pizza, meat and poultry, fruit, vegetable, and potato product segments. AFE has installed machines in the United States, Canada, Europe, and South America, and counts members of the US Poultry & Egg Association and the Midwest Food Processors Association among its industry connections.

The company states its mission is to deliver the most hygienic, energy-efficient, and reliable food processing equipment, backed by over 150 years of combined team experience. AFE emphasizes expert welding, sanitary design, rapid installation (often within days), and a comprehensive spare-parts inventory to minimize downtime.

name: Advanced Food Technologies
old_description: We are a world-class manufacturing partner that utilizes entrepreneurial ingenuity, thoughtful partnership, and uncompromising safety and quality standards to deliver trust-fueled brand growth.
about:
Advanced Food Technologies, operating as Roskam Foods, is headquartered in Grand Rapids, Michigan. Founded in 1923 as a single-product operation, the company has grown into one of the largest multi-category external food manufacturers in the United States. The business is investor-backed and employs approximately 2,400 people across eight facilities in the U.S. and Canada.

The company provides co-manufacturing services for branded food companies, national retailers, and private-label partners. Its processing platforms include twin- and single-screw extrusion for direct-expanded cereals, protein crisps, and snack puffs; end-to-end baking with dough mixing, sheeting, proofing, baking, and tempering; specialty snack processing such as drying, seasoning, air popping, and particulate application; and advanced packaging in stand-up pouches, dual-compartment cups, bag-in-box, and bulk super-sacks. In-house engineering supports feasibility studies, line design, capital assessments, and turnkey capital project management. The combined footprint exceeds two million square feet of manufacturing and warehouse space with more than 50 production and packaging lines.

Roskam serves the snack food, confectionery, frozen meal, pizza dough, dry baking mix, cereal, and granola categories. Its five specialized platforms—Baked Snacks & Popcorns, Frozen Foods, Dry Mix Blending, Cereal & Granola, and Confectionary—span frozen, refrigerated, and shelf-stable temperature states. Customers include national brands, store-brand programs, and private-label partners seeking large-scale, multi-category production consolidation.

The company emphasizes a partner-first mindset, disciplined execution, and continuous investment in new technologies and formats. All facilities hold SQF Level II and III certification, with additional USDA Organic, Non-GMO Project Verified, Keto Certified, Fair Trade, and Kosher certifications. Dedicated peanut-free facilities and controlled allergen protocols address sensitive ingredient handling. Integrated R&D, packaging development, supply chain logistics, and project management support take concepts from ideation through commercialization.

about:
Advanced Packaging Solutions & Products, Inc. was founded in January 2012 in Summerville, South Carolina, by two Clemson University packaging engineers, Dwayne Rainey and Nick Young.

The company operates an in-house wood shop producing CAD-designed custom crates, pallets, skids, and CNC-cut lumber, while also distributing over 20,000 stock packaging items — including corrugated boxes, foam, poly bags, stretch film, tape, and labels — from warehouses in Chicago, Dallas, Hazelton, Atlanta, and other cities. Services encompass kitting and fulfillment, vendor-managed inventory (VMI), on-site packaging, military-spec packaging, and consultative engineering available on an hourly or project basis.

Customers span e-commerce, food and beverage, industrial manufacturing, medical and pharmaceutical, agriculture, automotive, chemical, commercial, and distribution sectors. The firm serves businesses needing both off-the-shelf supplies and engineered packaging solutions, such as custom wood crates for heavy equipment or mil-spec packaging for defense items.

The founders started the business to provide engineering-driven packaging optimization, combining custom manufacturing with a broad stock portfolio to reduce lead times and total packaging cost for clients.

name: Advanced Plastics
old_description: Since 1959, Advanced Plastics has served as a quality wholesale distributor of fiberglass reinforced plastics, cast polymers, sign supplies and thermoplastics.
about:
Advanced Plastics, headquartered in Nashville, Tennessee, was founded in 1959 as a wholesale distributor of fiberglass reinforced plastics, cast polymers, sign supplies, and thermoplastics. The company operates eight stocking distribution centers across Tennessee, Alabama, Missouri, Louisiana, and Texas, serving customers from a network that includes branches in Memphis, Knoxville, Chattanooga, St. Louis, Birmingham, Elberta, New Orleans, and Arlington.

The business is organized into two divisions. The Composites Division supplies fiberglass reinforced plastics and related materials to the marine, transportation, corrosion, aerospace, construction/architectural, cast polymer, and advanced composites markets. The Sign Supply and Plastics Division provides sign-making materials, digital printing substrates, glazing products, and industrial thermoplastics to the quick-sign, digital printing, and industrial plastics sectors. Advanced Plastics positions itself as a wholesale distributor that maintains sufficient inventory to serve large manufacturers while remaining responsive to smaller accounts.

Customers span a range of industries including marine, transportation, aerospace, construction, cast polymer manufacturing, advanced composites, digital printing, sign fabrication, glazing, and general industrial plastics. The company works with both major manufacturers and smaller fabricators, offering product selection across composites, cast polymers, sign supplies, and thermoplastics.

Advanced Plastics emphasizes its scale and agility, stating it is "large enough to partner with major manufacturers, yet nimble enough to offer exceptional support to customers of all sizes." Membership in the American Composites Manufacturers Association and the International Cast Polymer Association reflects its industry engagement.
